Quick update from infra: we've identified a recent reconciliation job (2027-02-15T01:03Z) that applied a stale quota mapping to the customer. For tenant acme-analytics the burst window cap was set to 250 rps instead of the expected 2,500 rps due to a lookup fallback hitting an older snapshot. The job ran during maintenance and did not trigger a canary.

What we saw in the logs:
- 2027-02-15T08:46:12 PST: first 429s appear when burst queue fills
- Error pattern matches quota-exceeded on per-tenant-burst-cap
- No upstream failures observed; kernel traces show normal serving

Immediate mitigation steps already started:
1) Rollback the reconciliation snapshot (in progress).
2) Apply a temporary override to restore 2,500 rps for acme-analytics for the next 6 hours.
3) Enable extra logging for the tenant to capture rate / retry metrics.

Attachments: tenant-config-diff.json (diff between expected and applied config). I'll push a fix for the reconciliation lookup within the hour.

Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden 429s during nightly ingest (started 08:45 PST) — rollback complete

Rollback and override completed at 11:02 PST. Observed metrics:
- 429 rate dropped from 11.8% to <0.2% within 2 minutes.
- Ingest throughput returned to expected levels; no queue backlog remains by 11:20 PST.

Root cause summary (preliminary):
- A reconciliation lookup used an older index when a CDN cache miss occurred; the fallback returned a snapshot with stale caps.
- No code change in customer workload; this is an infra-side regression.

Next actions (tracking):
- Short-term: tighten reconciliation canary checks and prevent maintenance job from using last-resort snapshot (assigned to Marcus).
- Medium-term: introduce a unit test for reconciliation index freshness (assigned to Monica).
- Customer-facing: postmortem & credit for failed tokens (Evelyn) — target doc by 2027-02-18 and a postmortem call 2027-02-18 10:00 PST.

I'll attach the config diff and logs to the postmortem doc.

Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident update & next steps — Acme nightly ingest 2027-02-15

Hi Oliver,

Thank you again for the report and for bearing with us while we investigated. Summary and next steps below.

What happened (summary):
- On 2027-02-15 during your nightly ingest, a reconciliation job applied a stale quota snapshot to tenant acme-analytics that reduced the burst cap by 90% (250 rps vs expected 2,500 rps). That produced 429 responses as your job reached the lowered cap.

What we did:
- Immediately rolled back the reconciliation snapshot and applied a 6-hour override to restore normal throughput. Rollback completed 2027-02-15 11:02 PST.
- Implemented extra tenant-level logging to validate recovery.
- Issued token credits for failed requests from the ingest window.

Remediation plan & timeline:
- Fix reconciliation lookup to prefer fresh index and add a hard fail for last-resort snapshots — target complete 2027-02-22.
- Add canary gating for reconciliation jobs during maintenance windows — target complete 2027-02-24.
- Postmortem document: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c_postmortem_acme_429 (draft shared).

We have scheduled a short postmortem call to walk through details and answer questions: 2027-02-18 10:00 PST (calendar invite: https://calendar.redwoodinference.com/event/20270218-acme-postmortem).

If you'd like us to expand the temporary override window or provide additional telemetry exports from the ingest run, let me know and we'll arrange it.

Apologies for the disruption; we value Acme Analytics and will use this incident to improve our reconciliation safety checks.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
